rounds.text: Share India Securities Ltd trades at a compelling P/E ratio of 11.6x [E1], which sits well below the sector benchmark of 19.73x [E6], while offering exceptional historical growth highlighted by a 10-year compounded sales growth of 35% [E14] and profit growth of 48% [E18]. The company's profitability and capital efficiency dramatically outpace sector benchmarks, demonstrated by an ROA of 7.94% versus the 1.89% sector norm [E8], an ROE of 12.28% against 4.9% [E9], and an ROCE of 17% compared to just 5.12% [E10]. This fundamental outperformance is underscored by a rules-based screen score of 84 out of 100 yielding a BUY signal [E64], driven by robust recent metrics such as trailing twelve-month profit growth of 18% [E21] and a surging quarterly operating margin of 45% in June 2026—a 5 percentage point expansion year-over-year [E30]. conceded: [E33], [E34], [E35], [E61].

Despite seemingly attractive valuation multiples, Share India Securities Ltd carries substantial hidden risks and structural warning signs that undermine the bull thesis. Most alarmingly, the company suffers from severe cash flow destruction, generating negative operating cash flow of Rs -182 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -186 Cr for March 2026, resulting in a deeply distressed cash conversion ratio of -0.56x [E33, E34, E35]. This financial strain is compounded by a massive contingent liabilities burden of Rs 6,466 Cr and an expanding borrowing footprint, with total borrowings rising to Rs 695 Cr alongside flagged high borrowing costs [E38, E60, E62]. Furthermore, corporate governance and insider confidence appear questionable as promoters have steadily reduced their stake over the last three years by -4.19% down to 48.62%, with a concerning 40.4% of their remaining holding pledged [E40, E61, E63]. Underlying momentum is also visibly stalling, evidenced by a complete stagnation in 3-year compounded profit growth at 0%, declining operating margins over the TTM period, and decelerating earnings accompanied by negative institutional money flows [E20, E29, E43, E69]. Conceded: the company displays strong historical long-term sales growth, a low headline price-to-earnings multiple, and an impressive multi-year return on equity profile [E1, E14, E26].

Conceded: operating cash flow was negative Rs -182 Cr and free cash flow was negative Rs -186 Cr for March 2026 [E34, E35]. However, the business maintains a comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 2.25x and conservative financing with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.26x [E36, E37]. While borrowings increased to Rs 695 Cr, the company demonstrates exceptional operational profitability, outperforming sector benchmarks with an ROA of 7.94% versus 1.89%, an ROE of 12.28% versus 4.9%, and an ROCE of 17% versus 5.12% [E8, E9, E10, E38]. On margins, although the TTM operating margin saw a minor contraction, quarterly operating margins rebounded strongly to 45% in June 2026 compared to 40% in the year-ago quarter [E29, E30]. Furthermore, despite promoter stake reductions and pledging, the company trades at a highly discounted P/E of 11.62x against a sector benchmark of 19.73x and an EV/EBITDA of 2.98x against 13.49x [E6, E11, E40, E61, E63]. Finally, the intrinsic undervaluation is robustly supported by a reverse DCF showing the current price implies a mere 0.7% growth rate, while historical performance boasts a 10-year compounded profit growth of 48% [E18, E46].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 11.62x against a sector benchmark of 19.73x and an EV/EBITDA of 2.98x against 13.49x [E6, E11]. However, this low valuation is entirely warranted by severe fundamental deterioration, evidenced by compounded profit growth over 3 years flatlining at 0% and explicit signals that earnings growth is decelerating [E20, E69]. While the bull highlights an ROA of 7.94% and ROCE of 17% [E8, E10], these metrics mask a deeply alarming cash generation failure where operating cash flow plunged to Rs -182 Cr and free cash flow dropped to Rs -186 Cr in March 2026, driving cash conversion down to an abysmal -0.56x [E33, E34, E35]. Furthermore, the bull's reliance on a June 2026 margin rebound [E30] ignores the broader structural trend of an inconsistent yearly operating margin profile and a TTM contraction of 4 percentage points [E29, E31]. The claim of conservative financing [E36] is undermined by borrowings surging from Rs 513 Cr to Rs 695 Cr alongside a high cost of borrowing [E38, E62]. Finally, insider confidence is heavily compromised, as promoters have actively decreased their holding over the last 3 years by 4.19%, pledged 40.4% of their remaining shares, and left the business burdened by massive contingent liabilities of Rs 6,466 Cr [E60, E61, E63].

Conceded: compounded profit growth over 3 years flatlined at 0% [E20], operating cash flow was Rs -182 Cr alongside free cash flow of Rs -186 Cr in March 2026 [E34, E35], and promoter holding decreased over 3 years by 4.19% [E63]. However, the bear's claim of severe fundamental deterioration ignores robust 10-year and 5-year compounded profit growth of 48% and 32% respectively [E18, E19], alongside a strong trailing twelve-month profit growth of 18% [E21] and a recent quarterly operating margin expansion of 5 percentage points [E30]. Conceded: borrowings rose to Rs 695 Cr [E38] and contingent liabilities stand at Rs 6,466 Cr [E60], but the company maintains a comfortable short-term current ratio of 2.25x [E37] and a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.26x [E36]. Furthermore, the valuation remains exceptionally compelling because the stock trades at a deep discount with a P/E of 11.6x against the sector benchmark of 19.73x [E1, E6] and an EV/EBITDA of 2.98x against 13.49x [E11]. Finally, the business delivers a superior return on capital employed of 17% compared to the sector benchmark of 5.12% [E10] and boasts a stellar relative-strength rating of 100 [E50].

Conceded: the company displays 10-year and 5-year compounded profit growth of 48% and 32% [E18, E19], a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 18% [E21], a recent quarterly operating margin expansion of 5 percentage points [E30], a current ratio of 2.25x [E37], a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.26x [E36], a P/E of 11.6x against a 19.73x sector benchmark [E1, E6], an EV/EBITDA of 2.98x against 13.49x [E11], an ROCE of 17% [E10], and a relative-strength rating of 100 [E50]. However, pointing to long-term profit growth obscures severe medium-term stagnation, as 3-year compounded profit growth flatlined at 0% [E20] and 3-year compounded share price growth dropped by -13% [E23]. While the bull dismisses cash generation concerns, operating cash flow collapsed to negative Rs -182 Cr alongside free cash flow of negative Rs -186 Cr in March 2026, driving cash conversion to a dismal -0.56x [E33, E34, E35]. Furthermore, borrowings escalated to Rs 695 Cr [E38], contingent liabilities loom large at Rs 6,466 Cr [E60], and promoter commitment is actively retreating through a 4.19% holding decrease over 3 years [E63] alongside 40.4% of promoter shares being pledged [E61]. Finally, institutional money flow registers negative (-0.17 percentage points holding change) [E43], exposing a clear institutional exit that invalidates the bull's superficial reading of valuation multiples.
